Subject: Redwood Private / VPC evaluation — next steps and tests

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

- Recap: Acme wants a private deployment (VPC or on-prem) for PII-sensitive workloads, control-plane isolation, and an air-gapped option for regulated clients. Key evaluation criteria you flagged: network design (egress/ingress), control-plane connectivity, key management (KMS/HSM), and ability to run a constrained POC (throughput/latency/accuracy).

- Immediate next steps (proposed):
  1) Tech POC scope: 2-week sandbox running our private agent in your VPC or on an air-gapped subnet. Tests: 99th-pctl latency, steady-state throughput (tokens/sec), cold-start, KV cache effectiveness, and end-to-end request path (control plane vs offline mode)
  2) Security info: I'll attach our private/VPC overview and the networking checklist for your infra team to review.
  3) Procurement: sample SOW + pricing draft attached for planning.
  4) Timeline: kickoff engineering sync next Tue (2026-03-10) if that works for you.

Can you confirm the following so we can lock the POC plan?
- Which environment do you want to try first: VPC peering in your AWS account or fully air-gapped on-prem?
- Who should I loop for networking (CIDR, NAT/GW, egress restrictions) and your security lead for controls review?
- Any hard constraints on external control-plane reachability (e.g., no outbound at all vs allow limited management egress)?

Attaching the overview and checklist — happy to walk through these with your engineers.

Best,
Marissa

Marissa —

Thanks for the concise recap. A few clarifying items from our side before we lock the POC:

1) Preference: start with VPC peering in our AWS account. If that goes well we will discuss air-gapped on-prem for a subset of customers.
2) Networking: I'll loop in our infra lead (eng-team@acme-corp.com). We have strict egress controls; we prefer a limited control-plane egress to a allowlisted Alpine endpoint (will share IP ranges).
3) Security: our security team (security@acme-corp.com) has a few initial asks:
   - Do you support customer-managed KMS for model keys and logs encryption?
   - Can the control plane be hosted in our VPC or does it require Redwood-managed control plane access over the internet?
   - What support do you offer for fully air-gapped installs (install package, offline telemetry, update process)?
4) Competitive comparison: We are evaluating hyperscaler offerings (AWS Bedrock + SageMaker Inference) and another inference API vendor. Can you summarize the 2–3 differentiators for Redwood Private vs hyperscalers (network isolation, cost predictability, rollout/ops) — a slide or one-pager would help.

We'll aim to get networking details and IP ranges by EOD Thursday.

— Alex

Quick follow-ups from security (copying security@):
- KMS: must be customer-managed (bring your own key) for model encryption at rest.
- Audit logs: we need continuous logging of inference requests (token-level costs redacted) and an option to ship logs to our SIEM (Splunk).
- Control plane: preferred option is a customer-hosted control plane or a strongly allowlisted Redwood management endpoint. For air-gapped installs, we need an offline installer and a documented update process that does NOT require internet access during install.

Competitive question for your internal team: why would we pick Redwood Private over Bedrock/SageMaker if we already run on AWS (concerns: vendor lock-in vs specialized inference stack)? Looking for succinct bullets we can present to execs.

Alex —

Attached is a concise POC plan and the private/VPC overview and networking checklist you can share with eng/security. High-level answers to your asks below, and I'll follow up with the one-pager Rishi is drafting by EOD.

- KMS: We support customer-managed KMS keys (BYOK). For air-gapped installs you can integrate with an on-prem HSM; we have a documented flow for key injection during install.
- Audit logs: We can stream audit logs to your SIEM (Splunk) via a push or pull connector. Logs can be redacted to remove token-level content per your compliance needs.
- Control plane options: three supported topologies:
  1) Redwood-managed control plane (default): lightweight management endpoints; requires allowlisted egress.
  2) Customer-hosted control plane: we ship a control-plane bundle you run in your VPC (no external egress needed for management).
  3) Fully air-gapped: installer bundle + offline package for updates; recommended for regulated customers.

- Why Redwood Private vs hyperscalers (short bullets you can use for execs):
  • Deployment flexibility: identical API/ops across hosted, dedicated, and private — you can start with VPC and later move to air-gapped without replatforming.
  • Inference economics: specialized runtime + batching/kv caching leads to lower token cost for production LLM workloads vs general-purpose cloud endpoints.
  • Production tooling: first-class rollout/rollback, traceable evals, and per-route cost/latency dashboards tailored to inference workloads.
  • Control & compliance: BYOK, customer-hosted control plane option, and documented air-gapped install flow with HSM support.

POC scope (attached):
- Week 0: infra review + access (CIDRs, allowlist ranges)
- Week 1: deploy private agent in your VPC (peered) with sample model, run baseline latency/throughput tests
- Week 2: run resilience tests (restart/cold starts), KV cache benchmark, and SIEM log integration test

Next sync: propose Tue 2026-03-10 10:00 AM PT for kickoff engineering call. I can include Rishi and our infra lead.
